map_coordinates.note: Relatively compact battlefield for divisional operations

key_terrain_features.name: Halfaya Pass ('Hellfire Pass')
key_terrain_features.description: Narrow winding pass through 200m escarpment between coastal plain and desert plateau. Only vehicle route connecting coast with interior for 30km north-south.
key_terrain_features.strategic_importance: CRITICAL - controls access between coast and desert. Whoever holds pass controls movement in sector.

tactical_features.gradient: Steep switchbacks - vulnerable to fire from above
tactical_features.observation: Commanding observation over approaches from both east and west
tactical_features.fields_of_fire: Excellent - guns positioned on escarpment can fire down length of pass

key_terrain_features.defender: Axis - 5. leichte Division battlegroup under Hauptmann Wilhelm Bach
key_terrain_features.fortifications: Concrete bunkers, minefields, wire, dug-in 88mm FlaK guns
key_terrain_features.historical_significance: German 88mm guns positioned here destroyed 50+ British tanks over 3 days. Earned nickname 'Hellfire Pass' from British. Bach's defense made him legendary.
key_terrain_features.attackers: 4th Indian Division with Matilda tank support (June 15)
key_terrain_features.outcome: Axis held - British attack repulsed with heavy tank losses

key_terrain_features.name: Fort Capuzzo
key_terrain_features.description: Italian colonial fortress built pre-war. Concrete bunkers, underground galleries, barbed wire perimeter, minefields.
key_terrain_features.strategic_importance: HIGH - controls junction of coastal road and desert tracks. Observation point.

tactical_features.fortification_type: Permanent concrete fortifications - bunkers, casemates, trenches

key_terrain_features.historical_action: Captured by 4th Indian Division June 15. Recaptured by German counterattack June 16. Changed hands multiple times.
key_terrain_features.outcome: Axis retained at end of battle

key_terrain_features.name: Hafid Ridge
key_terrain_features.description: Low rocky ridge 30-50m high running north-south for 8km. Provides observation and hull-down firing positions for armor.
key_terrain_features.strategic_importance: HIGH - key defensive terrain for German mobile reserves

tactical_features.observation: Excellent observation over surrounding desert for 15-20km
tactical_features.tank_terrain: Excellent hull-down positions. Rocky ground provides cover.
tactical_features.concealment: Reverse slopes provide concealment for reserves

key_terrain_features.historical_action: 15. Panzer positioned here launched devastating counterattack June 16-17 against British 7th Armoured Division. British tank attack on ridge repulsed.
key_terrain_features.outcome: Axis held - British armor suffered heavy losses attacking ridge

key_terrain_features.name: Point 206
key_terrain_features.description: Hill mass rising 206m above sea level. Highest terrain in area.

tactical_features.observation: Excellent 360° observation - can see entire battlefield

key_terrain_features.historical_action: British attempted capture for observation. Limited fighting.

key_terrain_features.name: Sollum
key_terrain_features.description: Small coastal town at foot of escarpment. Port and road junction.
key_terrain_features.facilities: Small port, coastal road junction, water sources
key_terrain_features.historical_action: Not directly attacked - British focused on Halfaya Pass

key_terrain_features.name: Sidi Omar
key_terrain_features.description: Desert track junction and minor fort. Open desert terrain.
key_terrain_features.strategic_importance: LOW - flanking route for British maneuver
key_terrain_features.historical_action: British 7th Armoured Division maneuvered through this area attempting to outflank Axis positions. Engaged German mobile reserves.
key_terrain_features.outcome: Scene of mobile tank battles June 16-17

key_terrain_features.name: Bardia
key_terrain_features.description: Major Italian colonial fortress town and port. Scene of heavy fighting in Operation Compass (January 1941).
key_terrain_features.facilities: Port, extensive fortifications, supply dumps, water
key_terrain_features.historical_action: Not attacked during Battleaxe - outside operational area. British objective for exploitation if offensive succeeded.

terrain_analysis.overall_terrain_type: Rocky desert plateau with escarpment separating coastal plain from interior

trafficability.coastal_plain: GOOD - relatively flat, firm sand and gravel. Suitable for all vehicles.
trafficability.desert_plateau: EXCELLENT - firm rocky desert. Ideal tank country. Open maneuver terrain.
trafficability.escarpment: IMPASSABLE except at passes (Halfaya main pass, minor tracks). Steep cliffs 150-200m high.
trafficability.wad is: DIFFICULT - dry riverbeds with steep banks. Obstacle to vehicles.

observation_and_fields_of_fire.escarpment_top: EXCELLENT - 20-30km visibility in clear conditions. Dust plumes visible 40+km.
observation_and_fields_of_fire.desert_plateau: EXCELLENT - flat open terrain. Long-range observation and gunnery possible.
observation_and_fields_of_fire.coastal_plain: GOOD - relatively flat with some undulation.
observation_and_fields_of_fire.mirage_effect: SEVERE - heat shimmer distorts observation beyond 2km in midday

concealment_and_cover.general: POOR - very limited natural concealment in open desert
concealment_and_cover.ridges_and_wadis: MODERATE - reverse slopes and wadi banks provide some cover
concealment_and_cover.fortifications: GOOD - prepared positions at Halfaya, Capuzzo provide excellent cover

man_made: Minefields (extensive at Halfaya Pass, Fort Capuzzo, defensive positions)

via_balbia.condition: Good paved road - main Axis supply route
via_balbia.tactical_significance: Main axis of communication for Axis forces

desert_tracks.routes: Network of tracks connecting interior positions
desert_tracks.condition: Fair - marked by oil drums and cairns. Easily lost.
desert_tracks.navigation: Difficult - compass and dead reckoning essential
desert_tracks.tactical_significance: British maneuver routes for flanking movements

halfaya_pass_road.capacity: Very limited - single file vehicles, easily blocked
halfaya_pass_road.tactical_significance: CRITICAL - only vehicle pass for 30km. Whoever controls pass controls movement.

water_sources.natural: NONE - completely arid zone. No surface water.
water_sources.tactical_impact: Both sides dependent on trucked water. No local procurement possible. Water supply critical limiting factor.

axis_defensive_line.concept: Fortified positions (Halfaya, Capuzzo) anchored defense. Mobile reserves (15. Panzer) positioned centrally for counterattack.

desert_flank.objective: Outflank Axis via Sidi Omar, engage German reserves
desert_flank.outcome: Engaged 15. Panzer at Hafid Ridge - repulsed with losses

british_attacks: 4th Indian Division assaults Halfaya Pass (REPULSED - 88mm guns)
7th Armoured Division advances toward Hafid Ridge (ENGAGED German reserves)
day_1_june_15.axis_response: 5. leichte holds Halfaya. 15. Panzer deploys to Hafid Ridge to block British armor.
day_1_june_15.key_terrain: Halfaya Pass - German 88mm guns destroyed 30+ British tanks

british_attacks: 7th Armoured attacks Hafid Ridge (REPULSED - heavy tank losses)
day_2_june_16.axis_counterattacks: 15. Panzer counterattacks from Hafid Ridge. Recaptures Fort Capuzzo. British armor suffering heavy attrition.
day_2_june_16.key_terrain: Hafid Ridge - German tanks in hull-down positions defeated British armored attack

day_3_june_17.british_withdrawal: XIII Corps withdraws to Egypt. Offensive failed. Lost 91 tanks (50% of force).
day_3_june_17.axis_pursuit: Limited - fuel shortages prevented pursuit. Rommel wanted to exploit but logistics prevented.
day_3_june_17.outcome: Axis tactical and operational victory. British withdrawn. Tobruk remains besieged.

artillery_positions: Halfaya Pass: 88mm FlaK in AT role (German) - CRITICAL
British: Mobile artillery following armor divisions

scenario_maps.tactical_scale: 15km x 15km - Halfaya Pass sector OR Hafid Ridge sector
scenario_maps.skirmish_scale: 5km x 5km - Fort Capuzzo assault OR Halfaya Pass defenses
